Hi Maya / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a short set of ask items so we can size a focused Dedicated pilot that validates the SLOs you described. I captured what we heard and a proposed validation approach below.

What we heard (call highlights)
- Target latency goals: p50 ~ 60-100ms, p95 target ~ <=250ms for interactive flows.
- Peak concurrency: bursts up to ~120 concurrent user sessions, steady-state ~30–45 concurrent.
- Streaming: yes, low-latency streaming required for the conversational UI; partial tokens must start returning within 40–60ms for the first chunks.
- Typical request shape: average input ~120 tokens, output ~80 tokens; 1.5–2.0k model tokens/sec budget on sustained load.
- Model preference: open-weights Llama-fam variant + a smaller faster variant for low-latency fallback.

Ask 1 — 3 quick clarifying datapoints (if you can reply in-line):
1) Confirm steady-state QPS vs peak bursts in requests/sec (not sessions) — you mentioned 200 rps bursts; is 220 the safe ceiling?
2) Any requests that are long-form generation (>=512 tokens) that we must validate with the same SLO?
3) Are there any geo restrictions (we should run pilot in us-west only) or compliance blocks (no cross-region caching)?

Proposed Dedicated pilot plan (high-level)
- Objective: validate p50/p95 latency and streaming-first-chunk behavior at 30/120 concurrency points and measure reserved throughput cost.
- Matrix: run targeted experiments across 3 GPU profiles (shortlist below), with both prefix-cached and cold-KV scenarios. Each run: 30 minutes at sustained load, then 3–5 minute burst window for tails.
- GPU shortlist we recommend testing: H100 (optimal tail latency for fp16), A100 80GB (good throughput for batching), and L4 (cost-efficient streaming variant).
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms and first-stream-chunk <= 60ms on the streaming path for the critical flow; throughput within 10% of modeled predictions.

Attachments: pilot_sizing_template.xlsx (please fill required peak numbers), I attached an example stream trace from a similar pilot.

Next steps
- If you can reply with the 3 datapoints above by EOD tomorrow we’ll draft a mutual action plan and a perf matrix with recommended reserved throughput and GPU mix.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute alignment with your ops on Wednesday — I’ll share times.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks Maya — that helps a lot. Based on your answers I sketched a concrete pilot and GPU-fit proposal below. Karthik / Ben / Laura looped for ops/eng sizing and procurement coordination.

Pilot proposal (concrete)
- Setup: 3 short runs per GPU profile (H100, A100-80GB, L4)
  - Run A: steady-state at 40 rps for 30m (warm cache),
  - Run B: 30m steady + controlled burst to 220 rps for 5m (to validate tail),
  - Run C: 15m cold-KV simulation to measure cache-warmed delta.
- Metrics we’ll record: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, first-stream-chunk latency distribution, token/s throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.

GPU fit guidance (initial recommendation)
- H100 (2x reserved nodes): primary for routes where p95 tail matters — fewer tokens, low-latency streaming.
- A100 80GB (1–2 nodes pooled): for batched high-throughput reranking and long-form generations where batching yields unit-cost benefits.
- L4 (1–2 nodes): run the streaming path as a cost-conscious fallback for non-critical sessions; good first-chunk behavior in our internal benchmarks.

Sizing / reserved throughput suggestion (engineering starting point)
- Reserve throughput to cover steady-state 50 rps with headroom, plus burst capacity policy to handle 220 rps spikes with automatic fallback to the A100 pool for bulk batching. This maps approximately to: 2 H100 reserved, 1 A100 pool node, 1 L4 node as a pilot starting point. We’ll refine after the first run.

Attachments I’ll prepare and send after you confirm the mutual action plan: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.docx and perf_matrix.csv (we’ll pre-fill with the template you supplied).
